title: Swell, Soma

words.gram: imperative, 2nd sg. active (final a lengthened in the Saṃhitā; pada भव)
words.role: main verb of the third clause

sandhi.rule: m before a vowel is kept and joined

morphology.note: the Saṃhitā lengthens the final a of the imperative (P. 6.3.135 (द्व्यचोऽतस्तिङः)); the pada form is भव.

translation.literal: Swell, O Soma; may vigour come together to you from all sides; be [present] at the gathering of strength.
translation.readable: Grow full, Soma; let strength flow into you from every side, and be with us where strength is gathered.

meaning: A gāyatrī verse to Soma, who is both the sacred drink and the Moon: it asks him to swell and grow full, to gather vigour from every side, and to be present where strength and nourishment are gathered. In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (4.2.7.4) it belongs to the building of the fire altar: the Kalpa, as Sāyaṇa reports, uses it when the sand is spread out on the altar, and Sāyaṇa explains that a verse in which Soma is the deity is used because Soma bears the seed. It is also Ṛgveda 1.91.16. The verse names Soma, and āpyāyasva ‘swell’ is the word for the waxing of the Moon. The use of the verse for a graha belongs to the later gṛhya tradition, not to the Veda: in its source it serves another rite (see the commentary).
in_the_rite: The first mantra of Soma’s step in the Navagraha sūktam, the graha’s own mantra.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: The setting, from the Kalpa as Sāyaṇa quotes it: «आ प्यायस्व समेतु त इति सिकता».

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Sāyaṇa: «हे सोम त्वमाप्यायस्व सर्वतो वर्धयस्य», «वाजस्यान्नस्य संगथे संगमने त्वं निमित्तं भव»; and on why a verse to Soma is used for spreading the sand: «सोमो देवता यस्यामृचि प्रतीयते सेयमृक्सौमी».

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: Metre gāyatrī. The Ṛgveda (1.91.16) reads वृष्ण्यम् for the Taittirīya’s वृष्णियम्.
